# TLS certificate verification disabled (Node.js)

`qualor:js/tls-verification-disabled` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-295](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/295.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A07:2025 Authentication Failures](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A07_2025-Authentication_Failures/), [A07:2021 Identification and Authentication Failures](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A07_2021-Identification_and_Authentication_Failures/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
Code that turns off TLS certificate verification in Node.js clients:

- `rejectUnauthorized: false` for an `https` request or `Agent` (also `https.globalAgent`),
  `tls.connect()`, `http2.connect()`, an axios `httpsAgent` or an undici dispatcher;
- the TLS options of other client libraries: `rejectUnauthorized: false` under an `ssl`, `tls` or
  `https` key (node-postgres `ssl`, also handed on by knex, and as a branch of a ternary; nodemailer
  `tls`; got `https`), and in the options of a `ws` client;
- MongoDB's `tlsAllowInvalidCertificates` or `tlsInsecure` set to `true`, as an option of the driver
  or Mongoose, or in a `mongodb://` connection string;
- `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED` set to `'0'` from the code.

A `ca` or `checkServerIdentity` option next to `rejectUnauthorized: false` does not make it safe and
is reported too.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Without verification the client accepts any certificate. The traffic is still encrypted, but to
whoever answers: anyone on the network path (a public Wi-Fi, a compromised router, a proxy) can
pose as the server, read the traffic and change it, including passwords and API tokens.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** verification is switched off to reach a service with an internal CA.

```javascript
const https = require('https');

const agent = new https.Agent({ rejectUnauthorized: false });

function getStatus(callback) {
  https.get('https://internal.example.com/status', { agent }, callback);
}

module.exports = { getStatus };
```

**Compliant:** the internal CA is trusted through the `ca` option, and verification stays on.

```javascript
const fs = require('fs');
const https = require('https');

const agent = new https.Agent({ ca: fs.readFileSync('/etc/ssl/certs/internal-ca.pem') });

function getStatus(callback) {
  https.get('https://internal.example.com/status', { agent }, callback);
}

module.exports = { getStatus };
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Keep the default verification: remove `rejectUnauthorized: false` and never set
  `NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0`.
- To trust a private CA, pass it as the `ca` option (or start Node with `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`).
- To pin a certificate, add a `checkServerIdentity` check and leave `rejectUnauthorized` on.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Node.js https
- Node.js tls
- Node.js http2
- axios
- undici
- node-postgres (pg)
- `ws`
- `nodemailer`
- Got
- MongoDB Node.js driver
- Mongoose

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- Options from another module, from a function parameter, or spread into the options
  (`{ ...insecureTls }`) are not followed, nor are options built first and given to a module
  required in place (`require('tls').connect(port, host, options)`).
- For the other libraries, a TLS object kept in its own variable and given by shorthand
  (`new pg.Pool({ ssl })`) is not followed, and an object under an `https` key is taken for TLS
  options also where the library has no such option (axios).
- A `checkServerIdentity` that accepts any host, or MongoDB's `tlsAllowInvalidHostnames`, while the
  chain is still verified (CWE-297) is not reported.
- The global agent or an `Agent` imported by name and changed after the import is not followed.
- A function parameter whose default is `false` (`function makeAgent(verify = false)`) is not
  reported.
- The bracket form `process.env['NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED'] = '0'` is matched as text: a
  constant on its right is missed, and the line is reported inside a block comment.
- A client that turns verification off and checks `tlsSocket.authorized` itself is still reported.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test files [`rules/js/tls/tls-verification-disabled.js`](../../../rules/js/tls/tls-verification-disabled.js) and [`rules/js/tls/tls-verification-disabled.ts`](../../../rules/js/tls/tls-verification-disabled.ts) hold every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/js/tls/tls-verification-disabled.yml`](../../../rules/js/tls/tls-verification-disabled.yml), added in version 2026.10.1.
